text:
alex: Heads-up — need a final decision on the Q4 hardware reserve playbook. Holiday surge forecasts pushed GPU-hour demand ~38% vs baseline. Can we lock in something this week?

priya: Agreed. Forecast looks real after running the per-customer throughput sims. We should decide H200 vs H100 mix, plus whether to reserve L40S for cheap inference where possible.

ken: Quick numbers from supply ops: H200 lead time ~24-30 weeks if we want guaranteed slots. H100 vendor window ~16-22 weeks. L40S is much shorter, ~6-10 wks, but limited availability in APAC (add ~4 wks).

maria: Cost tradeoff reminder: H200 yields ~1.8x throughput on our long-seq models at ~2.2x cost/hr vs H100. L40S is ~0.6x throughput for float32 workloads but 0.4x cost/hr — great for low-latency cached inference.

alex: So proposed hedging: place partial H200 reservation for 40% of projected Q4 peak, H100 for 40%, L40S for 20% as burst/edge. Thoughts? @ken can you confirm procurement lead times for APAC vs NA?

ken: Confirmed. APAC adds ~2-4 weeks to H200 orders and longer customs slippage. NA/EU shipping is stable. Recommend pushing NA reservations first and APAC as follow-ups. Also suggest staggered delivery windows to avoid large capacity on-ramps.

priya: Also consider spot/partner-burst for non-SLA workloads. We ran sims: with 25% spot bursting + aggressive KV cache prewarm, effective GPU-hours needed drop ~18% and median latency within SLO for most query mixes.

maria: One more lever — quantized weights + lower-precision kernels reduce H100 GPU-hours by ~12% in our evals. Might change the mix if we can validate quality across top 10 customers.

ops-bot: Reservation proposal draft uploaded: s3://redwood-prod/procurement/q4-reserve-draft-v2.csv (see table: region, sku, qty, eta-window).

alex: Nice. Ops-bot table looks like this snippet:```
region,sku,qty,eta_start,eta_end
NA,H200,120,2026-10-01,2027-04-01
EU,H100,160,2026-09-15,2027-02-15
APAC,L40S,80,2026-08-01,2026-11-01
```

priya: Action items: 1) Ken to confirm vendor hold/cancel penalties by EOD Thursday. 2) Maria to run quality gate on quantized configs for top 10 customers by Tuesday. 3) Alex + procurement to sign partial POs covering 50% of proposed H200 by Friday.

ken: Will do. Also flag: if H200 lead times push past 30 weeks we may need to shift to heavier H100 weighting and rely on model parallelism to hit throughput.

maria: +1 to that contingency. Also recommend reserving an extra 10% L40S capacity in APAC as buffer for regional latency-sensitive customers.

alex: Cool — sync in 48h. If procurement gives a hard ETA we buy the H200 tranche. :thumbsup:

priya: +:thumbsup: — adding a short playbook doc to the thread after we finalize numbers.

ops-bot: Note: procurement approval workflow requires finance sign-off for >$2M net capex.

ken: tagging @finance leads in the doc.

maria: tiny note — check cooling constraints in our EU rack pods before committing full H200 density in EU zone. Last thermal audit showed two pods at 85% headroom.

alex: Good catch. Ken, include thermal headroom check in the PO hold checklist.

priya: Ok, wrapping. Quick wins: reserve partial H200 in NA, verify quantization quality, enable spot bursting config in the test fleet. We'll iterate next week.

alex: Thanks all. Thread closed once POs submitted.
